questions.question: Sum of radius and diameter of a circle is equal to the length of a rectangle. Breadth of rectangle is 10 cm and area of rectangle is 210 sq. cm. Find the radius of circle.
questions.solution:

Radius + diameter = Length of rectangle

Breadth = 10 cm

Area of rectangle = 210 sq. cm

Formula Used:

Area of rectangle = (length) × (breadth)

Calculation:

**Let the radius be r.**

⇒ 2r + r = length

length = 3r

⇒ 3r × 10 = 210

⇒ r = 7 cm

**The answer is 7 cm.**

questions.question: The price of an item increases by 20% every year, with the difference between its prices at the end of the third year and the fourth year being ₹180, what was its price at the end of the first year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Annual increase = 20%

Difference between price at end of 4th year and 3rd year = 180

**Formula Used:**

Price after n years = Initial price × (1.20)ⁿ

Difference = Price₄ − Price₃

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let price at end of 1st year = P

⇒ Price at end of 3rd year = P × (1.20)²

⇒ Price at end of 4th year = P × (1.20)³

⇒ Difference = P × (1.20)³ − P × (1.20)²

⇒ Difference = P × (1.20)²(1.20 − 1)

⇒ Difference = P × (1.44)(0.20)

⇒ Difference = 0.288P

⇒ 0.288P = 180

⇒ P = 180 ÷ 0.288

⇒ P = 625

**∴ The correct answer is 625.**

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 36, 76, 61, 25, 15, 61, 97, 65 and 14 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Observations: 36, 76, 61, 25, 15, 61, 97, 65, 14

**Formula Used:**

Arithmetic Mean = (Sum of all observations) / (Number of observations)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Sum of observations = 36 + 76 + 61 + 25 + 15 + 61 + 97 + 65 + 14

⇒ Sum = 450

⇒ Number of observations = 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 450 / 9

⇒ Arithmetic Mean = 50

**The arithmetic mean of the observations is 50.**

questions.question: A vendor sold 15 items for 3600 and gained a profit of 20%. How many items should he sell for 4320 to make a profit of 8%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

15 items sold for 3600 → Profit = 20%

Find number of items sold for 4320 → Profit = 8%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + profit%)

Cost Price = SP ÷ (1 + profit%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 15 items = 3600 ÷ 1.20 = 3000

⇒ CP of 1 item = 3000 ÷ 15 = 200

⇒ For 8% profit: SP per item = 200 × 1.08 = 216

⇒ Number of items = 4320 ÷ 216

⇒ Number of items = 20

**∴ He must sell 20 items.**

questions.question: Find the single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 10%, 12% and 20%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply successive discount formula D = a + b − (a × b) / 100 %.

Combine 10% and 20% first for easier calculation: 10 + 20 − (10 × 20) / 100 = 30 − 2 = 28%.

Now combine 28% and the remaining 12%: 28 + 12 − (28 × 12) / 100 = 40 − 3.36 = 36.64%.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive discounts = 10%, 12%, and 20%

Let initial Marked Price (MP) = 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc3a8cc466b20b8d7b3d5dcea86954acd80636c2ef763daf12da4741802e61ef.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − d₁ / 100) × (1 − d₂ / 100) × (1 − d₃ / 100)

Equivalent Discount % = ((MP − SP) ÷ MP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 100 × (1 − 10/100) × (1 − 12/100) × (1 − 20/100)

⇒ SP = 100 × (90/100) × (88/100) × (80/100)

⇒ SP = 100 × 0.90 × 0.88 × 0.80

⇒ SP = 90 × 0.88 × 0.80

⇒ SP = 79.2 × 0.80

⇒ SP = 63.36

⇒ Equivalent single discount = ((100 − 63.36) ÷ 100) × 100% = 36.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 36.64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When a series of discounts are given one after another on the progressively reduced price, it is called successive discount. The single equivalent discount is always less than the direct sum of the individual percentage discounts.

Discount Order Independence

The final equivalent single discount remains exactly the same regardless of the sequence in which the discounts are applied. Calculating 10%, then 20% gives the exact same Selling Price as calculating 20%, then 10%.

Multiplying Factor Method

Instead of calculating step by step subtractions, we find Selling Price directly using multiplying factors representing the remaining percentage: SP = MP × remaining%₁ × remaining%₂.
</p

questions.question: 2 men or 3 women can do a piece of work in 10 days. In how many days can 4 men and 3 women do the same work together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

2 men or 3 women can do a piece of work in 10 days.

We need to find in how many days 4 men and 3 women can do the same work together.

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of individual work

Efficiency = Total work ÷ Time

Combined Efficiency = Sum of individual efficiencies

Time = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency

**Calculation:**

Work done by 2 men in 10 days = 1 unit.

⇒ Work done by 2 men in 1 day = 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1 units.

⇒ Work done by 1 man in 1 day = 0.1 ÷ 2 = 0.05 units.

Similarly, work done by 3 women in 10 days = 1 unit.

⇒ Work done by 3 women in 1 day = 1 ÷ 10 = 0.1 units.

⇒ Work done by 1 woman in 1 day = 0.1 ÷ 3 ≈ 0.0333 units.

Now, for 4 men and 3 women:

Combined efficiency = (4 × 0.05) + (3 × 0.0333)

⇒ Combined efficiency = 0.2 + 0.1 = 0.3 units/day.

Total work = 1 unit (same work).

Time = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time = 1 ÷ 0.3 ≈ 10 ÷ 3 ≈ 3.33 days.

**∴ The correct answer is option (4) **

questions.question: A cylindrical tank of height 10 m and radius 5 m has a small circular cut of 0.5 m radius on its top surface. What would be the total surface area of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Height of the cylindrical tank (h) = 10 m.

Radius of the cylindrical tank (R) = 5 m.

Radius of the circular cut (r) = 0.5 m.

**Formula Used:**

Lateral surface area of the cylinder = 2πRh

Top circular area = πR²

Bottom circular area = πR²

Cut area to be subtracted = πr²

Total surface area = Lateral surface area + Bottom circular area + (Top circular area - Cut area)

**Calculation:**

Lateral surface area = 2 × π × 5 × 10 = 100π

Bottom area = π × 5² = 25π

Top area without the cut = π × 5² - π × 0.5²

= 25π - 0.25π = 24.75π

Total surface area = 100π + 25π + 24.75π

= 149.75π

Total surface area = (599π/4)

**Therefore, the total surface area of the tank is (599π / 4) square meters.**

questions.question: If B is 25% more than A, and C is 20% more than B, then what is A : C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the value of A be 100.

Since B is 25% more than A, B = 100 + 25 = 125.

Since C is 20% more than B, C = 125 + (20 / 100) × 125 = 125 + 25 = 150.

The ratio of A : C = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

B is 25% more than A.

C is 20% more than B.

**Method Used:**

Fractional representation of percentage increase.

 A : C = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25% expressed as a fraction = 1 / 4

⇒ B = A + (1 / 4) × A = 5 / 4 × A

⇒ Ratio of A / B = 4 / 5

⇒ 20% expressed as a fraction = 1 / 5

⇒ C = B + (1 / 5) × B = 6 / 5 × B

⇒ Ratio of B / C = 5 / 6

⇒ To find the overall ratio A : C, multiply the individual ratios:

⇒ A / C = (A / B) × (B / C)

⇒ A / C = (4 / 5) × (5 / 6) = 20 / 30 = 2 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Converting percentages directly to simplified fractions helps in speeding up ratio calculations. Always memorize common fractions like 25% = 1/4 and 20% = 1/5.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two sequential ratios a:b and b:c is calculated by multiplying them: (a/b) × (b/c) = a/c. This provides the direct relationship between the first and last terms.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple changes sequentially, you can multiply the base with successive scaling factors. For example: Final = Base × (1 + %1) × (1 + %2).
</p

questions.question: The average weight of 12 people is 65 kg. If one person leaves and the new average becomes 64.5 kg, what is the weight of the person who left?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weight of the left person = Old Average + (Remaining People × Decrease in Average)

Old Average = 65 kg, Remaining People = 11

Decrease in Average = 65 − 64.5 = 0.5 kg

Weight = 65 + (11 × 0.5)

Weight = 65 + 5.5 = 70.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average weight of 12 people = 65 kg

New average weight after 1 person leaves = 64.5 kg

 
 12 People | Average: 65 kg (Total: 780 kg)
 
 
 11 People | Avg: 64.5 kg

 
 1 Left

 

 

 
 Total: 709.5 kg
 ? kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total initial weight of 12 people = 12 × 65 = 780 kg

⇒ Total weight of remaining 11 people = 11 × 64.5 = 709.5 kg

⇒ Weight of the person who left = (Total initial weight) − (Total new weight)

⇒ Weight of the person who left = 780 − 709.5

⇒ Weight of the person who left = 70.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When a Person Joins

If a new person joins and the average increases, New Weight = Old Average + (New total people × Increase in average).

When a Person is Replaced

If one person is replaced by another and the average changes, Weight of New Person = Weight of Replaced Person ± (Total number of people × Change in average).

Weighted Average

When combining two groups, Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

questions.question: If sin A=(5)/(13), then find the value of (cos A-2tan A)/(sin A+3tan A).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the 5-12-13 triplet for sin A = 5/13, we get P = 5, H = 13, and B = 12.

Thus, cos A = 12/13 and tan A = 5/12.

Numerator = 12/13 − 2×(5/12) = (144 − 130) / 156 = 14/156.

Denominator = 5/13 + 3×(5/12) = (60 + 195) / 156 = 255/156.

Value = Numerator ÷ Denominator = 14/255.

**∴ The correct answer is 14/255.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A = 5/13

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle:

sin A = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

cos A = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

tan A = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65e3e67abbcf68b08518b68eb5e94ed338b7b17b07a6deb05f993a3b29e1ef4b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Perpendicular = 5 and Hypotenuse = 13

⇒ Base = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12

⇒ cos A = 12/13

⇒ tan A = 5/12

⇒ Numerator = cos A − 2×tan A = 12/13 − 2×(5/12) = 12/13 − 10/12

⇒ Numerator = (144 − 130) / 156 = 14/156

⇒ Denominator = sin A + 3×tan A = 5/13 + 3×(5/12) = 5/13 + 15/12

⇒ Denominator = (60 + 195) / 156 = 255/156

⇒ Required Value = (14/156) ÷ (255/156) = 14/255

**∴ The correct answer is 14/255.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

These are sets of three integers that strictly satisfy Pythagoras Theorem. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Trigonometric Identities

The most fundamental identity is sin² A + cos² A = 1, from which values of cos A can be directly determined without drawing a triangle.

Tangent Relation

The tangent of an angle can always be derived from sine and cosine using the relation tan A = sin A ÷ cos A.
</p

questions.question: A trader bought two articles for a total of 1560. He sold one at a loss of 20% and the other at a profit of 15%. If the selling price of both articles was the same, then what was the cost price of the article which he sold at 20% loss?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total CP = 1560

Article A sold at 20% loss

Article B sold at 15% profit

SP of both articles is same

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 − loss%)

SP = CP × (1 + profit%)

**Calculations:**

Let CP of article A = x

⇒ CP of article B = 1560 − x

SP of A = x × 0.8

SP of B = (1560 − x) × 1.15

Since SP same:

⇒ x × 0.8 = (1560 − x) × 1.15

⇒ 0.8x = 1794 − 1.15x

⇒ 0.8x + 1.15x = 1794

⇒ 1.95x = 1794

⇒ x = 1794 ÷ 1.95

⇒ x = 920

**∴ The cost price of the article sold at 20% loss = 920.**
